description.value: In this assessment, students complete a designed solution task under exam-style time constraints to simulate working to a real-world deadline. Students are given an Australia-based design scenario and follow the final stages of the design process to generate, revise, evaluate, and refine a solution. Evaluation of the design must explicitly demonstrate empathy skills, including consideration of user perspectives, cultural context, and social impact. This assessment focuses on students’ ability to apply ethical, culturally informed, and reflective thinking to design decisions.

context.value: In this unit, students develop an understanding of Australian and Aboriginal histories and cultures while building empathy as a core design skill. Students explore how culture, context, and lived experience influence design decisions, and examine the importance of ethical and respectful design when responding to Aboriginal perspectives. Through guided learning, students consider how designers can create solutions that acknowledge cultural significance, community needs, and social impact. The unit emphasises empathy, reflection, and responsible decision-making, encouraging students to design with awareness of Australia’s cultural diversity and shared histories.

authenticationStrategies.label: You will be provided class time for task completion.
You will produce sections of the final response under supervised conditions.
You will provide documentation of your progress.
Your teacher will collect copies of your response and monitor at key junctures.
Your teacher will collect and annotate a draft.
Your teacher will conduct interviews or consultations as you develop the response.
You must submit a declaration of authenticity.
You will produce summaries during your response preparation.
Your teacher will conduct interviews after submission to clarify or explore aspects of your response.
Your teacher will compare the responses of students who have worked together in groups.
Your teacher will ensure class cross-marking occurs.
